items.rule_or_skill: chronological_reading.md: first pass and simulation limits

current_evidence.observation: One primary source-order pass and three scoped passes were frozen; inherited transcript exposure remained, and the per-unit states were reconstructed after the complete reading.

items.mechanism_of_failure: Calling every perspective cold or independent would inflate the evidence; retrospective checks could silently overwrite the encounter log.
items.proposed_general_change: Preserve immutable first-pass files and hashes, disclose inherited exposure and scoped jumps, and append resolutions with their locators instead of editing the initial state.
items.transfer_test: Test a later-defined symbol and an answer-exposed exercise; in both cases preserve the original knowledge boundary.
items.exception: A simulated log is editorial evidence even when complete; it is not an observed human comprehension study.

items.mechanism_of_failure: A plausible first-impression complaint can turn into a false absence claim when a verifier inspects only its quoted trigger or summarizes too much context. Retrospective reconstruction increases this risk.
items.proposed_general_change: For every absence claim, inspect the preceding definition, the rest of its paragraph and its immediate mathematical continuation; classify already-present information separately from delayed information and optional reformatting. Remove a complaint when its proposed repair is already performed.
items.classification: better application of existing verification rule
items.transfer_test: Apply to a probability boundary case, a circuit invariant and a historical status caveat. Each should survive only if a specific unmet reader operation remains.
items.exception: A later explanation can resolve truth while leaving a real long-distance first-encounter cost; preserve that cost only with its exact later-resolution locator.
items.evidence_kind: Observed failure mode of this simulated review, not measured human learning

simulation_limits: The chronological reader is an AI model with generic mathematical knowledge and inherited project context.
The four perspectives are explicitly simulated; scoped specialists are not four independent full-paper blind readers.
No stopwatch timings or student comprehension outcomes were measured.
Coverage rows record inspection, not theorem certification; a row with no issue is not an approval.
No deliberate literature or prior-review lookup was made during each declared first-pass scope; inherited exposure is disclosed, and subsequent verification is separate.
The strict prospective per-sentence protocol was not satisfied. No contemporaneous state is recoverable for the 5276 individual units; reconstructed passage context must not be mistaken for one.
Many rough absence claims failed local-context verification. Their rejection is documented; frozen notes are retained as history and do not override the accepted findings.
